week|2026-08-17|fleet|.text:
The week's problem is service and the room, not food. 554 reviews at 4.84 with 20 negatives (3.6%), against 335 at 4.76 with 18 (5.4%). Maki 21 accounts for 96 of them at 4.94 in its opening week, so strip it out for a like for like read: 458 reviews at about 4.82 with 19 negatives (4.1%). The negative rate improved, the average barely moved.

Food quality logged 28 issues, exactly as last week, but the mix changed. Cold food fell from 7 to 2 while broth rose from 3 to 7, at Fountainbridge, Nottingham, Leicester, Soho and Manchester, "very thin and not at all creamy". Service rose from 6 issues to 14 and inattentive service from 3 to 7, with three reviews recording rudeness at Bath Street, Meadowhall and Maki 21. Noise and decor doubled from 4 to 8. There is one food safety mention, "a piece of PLASTIC in the soup" at Nottingham on 23/08/2026.

Owners: Executive Chef on broth spec at the five sites named. Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh on Fountainbridge. Inka Cheung on Nottingham and Meadowhall, both GM posts vacant. Recognition: Harvey at Manchester named in 60 reviews, Amidu at Shoreditch in 12, Leandra at Leeds in 8.

week|2026-08-17|region|Scotland & Newcas.text:
Quality first with service close behind, and it is concentrated at Fountainbridge. 74 reviews, average 4.70, 7 negatives (9.5%), against 76 at 4.59 and 11.8% last week. The average improved, but this is still the fleet's worst negative rate, close to three times the fleet's 3.6%.

Food quality logged 8 issues, 6 of them at Fountainbridge: general taste 3 and broth 2. A 1-star on 21/08/2026 says the spicy broth is "made with water and cayenne pepper", and a 2-star on 23/08/2026 calls the tonkotsu "very thin and not at all creamy" with the meat sinewy and fatty. Service logged 5 issues across Fountainbridge, Bath Street and Renfield. At Bath Street on 19/08/2026 a server laughed at a request for a spoon and a plate, asked "do you need that" and never brought them. Renfield had gyoza that "arrived cold" on 18/08/2026. Fountainbridge labour hours fell from 645.7 to 600.0 in a week carrying two service complaints, with sales 8.0% under target.

Newcastle, Aberdeen and SJQ Edinburgh all came in at 5.0, small numbers at all three. Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh own coaching and rota at Fountainbridge and Bath Street. David at Fountainbridge was still praised three times.

week|2026-08-17|region|North England & M.text:
The region is healthy and the issues sit at two sites. 244 reviews, average 4.88, 5 negatives (2.0%), against 124 at 4.88 and 1.6%. Manchester carried 195 of those at 4.93 and Leeds 22 at 4.95, so the volume gain is real and comes from sites already in the feed.

Nottingham is the priority: 17 reviews, 4.53, 2 negatives, with food quality at 5 issues, speed 3 and service 3. "Half an hour for someone to take our order", one guest's dish arriving an hour after the rest, and a 3-star on 23/08/2026 reporting "a piece of PLASTIC in the soup" alongside a salty, greasy broth. Labour hours there rose from 478.6 to 495.4 and efficiency moved from 69 red to 91 amber, so this is floor execution rather than cover. Meadowhall took a 1-star on 20/08/2026 over how an outside food policy was explained to a family, on 2 reviews. Leicester had one 2-star on tasteless broth and flavourless boiled chicken, small numbers.

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own Nottingham and Meadowhall while both GM posts are vacant, and the Executive Chef owns the plastic trace and the broth. Recognition: Harvey at Manchester named in 60 reviews, Leandra at Leeds in 8, Aiden at Manchester in 6.

week|2026-08-17|region|South England.text:
Read the headline with care. 236 reviews at 4.83 against 135 at 4.73, but 96 of those are Maki 21's opening week at 4.94. Strip it out and the region is 140 reviews at about 4.75 with 7 negatives (5.0%), against 135 at 4.73 with 7 (5.2%). Flat, so nobody here caused the lift and nobody should be credited with it.

On that base the problem is food quality, spread rather than concentrated. Soho's vegan ramen on 17/08/2026 drew "Soup too salty" and vegan meat with "the texture of cardboard", and a 3-star on 22/08/2026 had an egg overcooked and not made fresh. Shoreditch's vegan katsu was called "bland quorn fillets". Shoreditch's 1-star on 21/08/2026 is a 16:10 Friday arrival with the hours showing open and the kitchen closed for a team meeting. Southampton's 1-star on 21/08/2026 is sequencing and complaint handling, and its labour hours fell from 812.7 to 778.9 while covers rose.

Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own Shoreditch, Southampton and Maki 21, none of which has a permanent GM. Executive Chef on the vegan ramen and katsu spec. Marketing (Becca) on Shoreditch's posted hours. Recognition: Amidu at Shoreditch named in 12 reviews, Navin in 7, Elham at Maki 21 in 6.

week|2026-08-17|site|M3.text: 13 reviews, average 4.23, 3 negatives (23.1%), against 7 at 4.57. Food quality is 6 of the 9 issues, general taste 3 and broth 2. A 1-star on 21/08/2026 says the spicy broth is "made with water and cayenne pepper". A 2-star on 23/08/2026 calls the tonkotsu "very thin and not at all creamy", the meat sinewy and fatty. The other 2-star that day is service: no greeting, no water and a disputed 10% charge. Labour hours fell from 645.7 to 600.0, sales landed 8.0% under target and efficiency dropped from 98 to 87. Run the broth check with the Executive Chef now. On the GM this is one week, so watch rather than act: Rory Ferguson on the floor.

week|2026-08-17|site|M6.text: Small numbers, 5 reviews at an average of 4.4 with one negative, but this one needs acting on rather than watching. On 19/08/2026 a guest asked for an extra spoon and plate, the server laughed in their face, asked "do you need that" and never brought them. The same review calls the food lovely as always. Rudeness is not a coach over time item. Justyna Polak to establish who was on that shift and deal with it this week, with Óisín Patrick Darragh sighted on the outcome. Sales were 2.3% under target, hours were 359.5 against 368.8 and efficiency held at 95 green, so this is behaviour on the floor, not pressure.

week|2026-08-17|site|M16.text: 17 reviews, average 4.53, 2 negatives (11.8%), against 7 at 4.29. Food quality is 5 issues, speed 3 and service 3. A 2-star on 23/08/2026: "Half an hour for someone to take our order", then one guest's dish arriving an hour after everyone else had finished. A 3-star the same day reports "a piece of PLASTIC in the soup", a salty greasy broth and a disputed service charge. Log and trace that food safety mention with the Executive Chef now. Labour hours rose from 478.6 to 495.4 and efficiency went from 69 red to 91 amber, so this is floor process, not cover. The GM post is vacant: Inka Cheung and Amy Tang to put a named lead on shift.

week|2026-08-17|site|M18.text: 18 reviews, average 4.61, 2 negatives (11.1%), against 18 at 4.56, so flat rather than deteriorating, though the rate is three times the fleet's. Both negatives are food. The vegan ramen on 17/08/2026 drew "Soup too salty" and vegan meat with "the texture of cardboard". A 3-star on 22/08/2026 had an egg overcooked and not made fresh, water forgotten after being ordered, and later tables served first. Covers rose from 1,556 to 1,758 while labour hours edged down to 637.4, which fits the sequencing and attention complaints. Imre Balogh on pass sequencing and the drinks check, Executive Chef on the vegan ramen build. Wage improved from 28.44% to 24.51% and efficiency from 64 to 77, still red.

week|2026-08-17|site|M19.text: 57 reviews, average 4.70, 4 negatives (7.0%), against 25 at 4.72, so the rate rose on more than double the volume. One of the four is a third party delivery complaint and sits outside the restaurant. The 1-star on 21/08/2026 matters most: a 16:10 Friday arrival, hours showing open online and in the window, the team visibly in a meeting and the kitchen closed. That is fixable today. A 3-star on 18/08/2026 calls the vegan katsu "bland quorn fillets" and says the pink lighting made the menu hard to read. Amidu was named in 12 reviews and Navin in 7. With the GM post TBC, Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own the hours fix with Marketing (Becca).

week|2026-08-17|site|M20.text: 26 reviews, average 4.77, one negative, against 40 at 4.88. The single negative is worth reading in full: on 21/08/2026 a family had two meals arrive within minutes and the rest around 29 minutes later, a child's katsu was never started, the compensation was disputed and the guest felt they were treated differently. That is sequencing and complaint handling, not food. Labour hours fell from 812.7 to 778.9 while covers rose from 1,725 to 1,795, and the site is red on efficiency at 60 with wages at 29.36%. With no permanent GM, Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own it: a sequencing rule for tables with children, and a clear same day resolution standard.

month|2026-08|fleet|.text:
August 2026 is a food problem, not a service problem, and it is worst in the South. Food quality complaints rose from 107 in July to 158 on 1,889 reviews (1,740 in July), while service complaints moved only from 72 to 79. Taste and quality alone went 44 to 64, protein 17 to 26, and broth or soup stands at 15. The fleet average held at 4.74 against 4.75, but negatives rose from 5.4 per cent to 6.0 per cent, 114 reviews in all.

Seafood freshness is the sharpest signal and it crosses four sites: squid that "tasted rotten" at Lakeside, squid "frozen for too long" at Soho, squid "still had the membrane attached" at Manchester, and salmon that "smelled rotten" at Maki Nori. Steak drew 13 complaints against 23 praises, thin or overcooked at Soho, Shoreditch, Metrocentre and Maki 21. Both sit with the Executive Chef and supply chain, not with individual GMs.

Praise is still the larger story: 1,007 food mentions, 988 service mentions and Maki rolls praised 53 times. Recognise Harvey (Manchester, 70 mentions), Navin (Shoreditch, 40) and Elham (Maki 21, 19).

month|2026-08|region|Scotland & Newcastl.text:
Scotland and Newcastle carries the lowest average in the fleet and its problem is split between the kitchen and the bill. 409 reviews at 4.65 (310 at 4.60 in July), 41 negatives at 10.0 per cent against 10.3 per cent, so this is a stubborn level rather than a new slide.

Food quality complaints rose from 30 to 44, taste and quality 15 to 18, protein 8 and food served cold or lukewarm 5. The service charge is now the loudest single service theme: 9 mentions of the bill or service charge and three reviews saying a manager handled the complaint badly. One Renfield guest describes a "10% tip to the receipt without even asking".

Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh own two actions. First, one written line for every GM on how the service charge is announced before ordering and removed on request, worked at Renfield and Metrocentre first. Second, a coaching pass on attentiveness where guests had to chase drinks, cutlery and the bill. Aberdeen is the bright spot, 4.49 to 4.72 on 37 to 67 reviews. Recognise David (Fountainbridge, 8 mentions), Chris (Aberdeen, 7) and Harry (Newcastle, 5).

month|2026-08|region|North England & Mid.text:
The strongest region on the numbers, and the widest spread inside it. 565 reviews at 4.78 (385 at 4.72), 25 negatives at 4.4 per cent, down from 5.5 per cent. Manchester alone contributed 385 reviews at 4.86 with only 2.3 per cent negative, and Leeds turned round hard, 4.54 to 4.78 with negatives 10.7 per cent to 2.5 per cent.

The problems are concentrated in the two sites without a GM and in Leicester. Nottingham fell 4.77 to 4.60 with 18 food quality issues, including a piece of plastic found in soup on 23/08/2026 and gyoza "soft and almost raw tasting" on 04/08/2026. Meadowhall took two one star reviews, on 20/08/2026 and 24/08/2026, for lecturing a family over the outside food policy. Leicester dropped 4.71 to 4.34 with negatives at 15.6 per cent, driven by six inattentive service mentions and dirty tables.

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang should treat the two vacancies as the cause to test first, take the Nottingham foreign object to the Executive Chef, and agree one calm script for the outside food and allergen conversation. Recognise Harvey (Manchester, 70 mentions), Sam (Manchester, 16) and Rami (Nottingham, 8).

month|2026-08|region|South England.text:
South England is where the fleet's food problem sits. 915 reviews at 4.76 (1,045 at 4.80), 48 negatives at 5.2 per cent against 3.9 per cent, so the rate got worse while volume fell. Food quality complaints rose 52 to 72 and taste and quality 20 to 31, with cleanliness and ambience 18 to 25 and seven mentions of dirty premises.

Soho is the site to act on: 4.53 on 109 reviews, 11.9 per cent negative, 23 food quality issues and four hygiene mentions including "filthy and out of order toilets". Shoreditch is the site to watch: negatives went 1.5 per cent to 6.4 per cent and the average 4.86 to 4.69, with two reviews about the door being shut inside posted hours. Maki Nori improved to 4.72 but carries two fish freshness reports. Southampton held at 4.81 but its review count fell from 504 to 165, which is a collection problem for Becca, not a performance one.

Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own the Soho reset with the Executive Chef on broth seasoning and seafood, and the Shoreditch opening hours discipline. Recognise Navin (Shoreditch, 40 mentions), Elham (Maki 21, 19) and Jocelyn (Lakeside, 12).

month|2026-08|site|M1.text:
Nicolson has the lowest average in the fleet, 4.30 on 23 reviews, four negatives at 17.4 per cent. It was 4.52 and 14.3 per cent in July, so this is two months above 14 per cent, not one bad week.

Volume is low and no cause dominates: three food quality issues, two each on cleanliness, speed and service. The theme is comparison. Two reviews say the food is weaker than at other branches and a four star guest calls the site "noisier, more cramped and less clean than Fountainbridge".

Watch, do not act. Derrick Cheung owns food temperature, raised twice, and the entrance greet. Ka Ho should get more reviews collected here.

month|2026-08|site|M11.text:
Leicester went from a good month to a bad one. 32 reviews at 4.34 against 45 at 4.71, negatives 4.4 per cent to 15.6 per cent, more than double the fleet rate and the second lowest average in the fleet.

The cause reads as cover, not cooking. Six issues are inattentive or forgotten service, four are speed, two are dirty tables. A guest on 25/08/2026 writes "skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow", and a five star reviewer noted one server on the floor at peak.

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang should check the rota against covers first, then agree clearing and check back routines with Caroline and JJ. Watch into September, do not judge one month.

month|2026-08|site|M12.text: Newcastle closed August on 44 reviews at 4.70, up from 4.66 on 32 in July, with 5 negatives. The negative rate of 11.4% is close to double the fleet's 6.0%, although it has eased from 12.5% in July. Food quality carries 9 of the 15 issue mentions, protein 4 of them and general taste 3, with chicken ramen and rice bowl the dishes named most often. Two mentions are hours related: closed early, refused entry or hours wrong. Executive Chef on the protein spec, Matt Lee on the door and the listed hours, Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh on coaching. Praise is real: Harry 5 mentions, Georgia 3.

month|2026-08|site|M13.text:
Aberdeen is the best turnaround in Scotland. 67 reviews at 4.72 against 37 at 4.49, negatives 13.5 per cent to 7.5 per cent, and 37 service praise mentions.

Two kitchen items need closing. On 26/08/2026 a guest reports karaage arriving within sixty seconds, undercooked and greasy, with sticky menus and a dried out egg. Separately a five star guest records prawns labelled gluten free being fried in shared oil, with the meal comped. The second is an allergen control point, not a service recovery.

Executive Chef and BOH own fryer separation and karaage cook time. Joe Herera owns menu cleaning and plate clearing, raised twice. Recognise Chris (7 mentions), Peter (4) and Jezer (3).

month|2026-08|site|M14.text:
Meadowhall took two one star reviews for the same avoidable conversation. 45 reviews at 4.64 against 26 at 4.85, negatives 3.8 per cent to 8.9 per cent.

On 20/08/2026 and 24/08/2026 two families describe staff lecturing them condescendingly about outside food brought in for a young child, one adding that a follow up complaint email went unanswered. Two issues are logged as rude or unfriendly attitude. Three more are portion size, including a black garlic ramen with very little broth on 24/08/2026.

Rudeness and an unanswered complaint mean act, not watch, even on one month. The GM post is vacant, so Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own it: one polite agreed script, and a named person answering complaints.

month|2026-08|site|M15.text:
Metrocentre needs a service and value conversation. 58 reviews at 4.57 against 62 at 4.73, negatives 6.5 per cent to 12.1 per cent, twice the fleet rate.

Four complaints are price and four are taste, and they land together: one guest paid £72 and described tiny steak, grey noodles and poor karaage on 09/08/2026. Three more are inattentive service, one guest on 10/08/2026 chasing drinks, cutlery, tissues and the bill. On 28/08/2026: "they add a tip to the bill without consent".

Kieran Day owns check back and clearing. Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh should take the service charge script here first. No staff member was praised by name in August.

month|2026-08|site|M16.text:
Nottingham has a food safety item and no GM. 63 reviews at 4.60 against 154 at 4.77, negatives 4.5 per cent to 9.5 per cent, and 18 food quality issues on only 63 reviews.

A guest dining with a child found a piece of plastic in the soup on 23/08/2026. On 04/08/2026 another describes gyoza "soft and almost raw tasting" and chicken that tasted reheated. Four complaints concern broth, four concern protein.

Executive Chef and BOH own the foreign object investigation and the gyoza cook off this week. Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own the GM vacancy, the likeliest reason standards slipped. Reviews falling 154 to 63 needs Becca. Rami is praised in 8.

month|2026-08|site|M17.text: Lakeside finished August at 4.81 on 131 reviews, level with 4.82 on 152 in July, and its 4.6% negative rate sits below the fleet's 6.0%. The mix has moved: cleanliness and ambience now carries 5 mentions and 4 of those are noise, temperature, comfort or decor rather than hygiene. Food quality carries 7, general taste 4 of them, and there is one foreign object or food safety mention, which goes to the Executive Chef. Kei Cannon on the room and the seating, with Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty. Service is the strength here: 88 praise mentions, Jocelyn 12, Lera 10, Maddison 8. Watch, do not act.

month|2026-08|site|M18.text:
Soho is the fleet's problem site. 109 reviews at 4.53 against 4.72 in July, 13 negatives at 11.9 per cent against 7.8 per cent, and 23 food quality issues on a tenth of Manchester's volume.

Two faults repeat. Seasoning and stock: ten taste mentions, three on broth, ramen "incredibly salty" on 30/08/2026 and squid "frozen for too long" on 15/08/2026. Hygiene: four dirty premises mentions, a bar "covered in dirty glasses" on 08/08/2026 and out of order toilets on 25/08/2026.

Act, do not watch. Imre Balogh owns an evidenced daily cleaning sign off. Executive Chef owns a broth seasoning and seafood check here. Imi (7 mentions) and Ginger (5) hold service together.

month|2026-08|site|M19.text:
Shoreditch is the biggest single deterioration in the fleet. 203 reviews at 4.69 against 200 at 4.86, negatives 1.5 per cent to 6.4 per cent. Volume held, so this is real.

Twenty one of 34 issues are food quality: nine taste, three protein, three food served cold. A one star on 02/08/2026 calls the chashu "inedible due to toughness" and the broth all salt. The door also failed twice: the kitchen shut at 16:10 on 21/08/2026 for a team meeting inside posted hours, and a confirmed booking arrived to a closed restaurant on 28/08/2026.

The GM post reads TBC, so Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty carry this. Navin is praised in 40 reviews.

month|2026-08|site|M20.text:
Southampton is performing, with an allergen incident and a collection problem behind it. 165 reviews at 4.81 against 4.83, negatives 3.6 per cent, among the best rates in the fleet.

On 11/08/2026 coeliac guests were told the kitchen could accommodate them, waited fifteen minutes, then were told almost nothing was gluten free. Executive Chef owns what is genuinely gluten free, the GM owns what the greeting promises. Three other issues are staggered service, a 21/08/2026 review describing a child's katsu never started.

The bigger flag is volume: reviews fell from 504 in July to 165. That is a Becca collection question, not performance. Mia is praised in 9 reviews, Tinky in 6.

month|2026-08|site|M3.text:
Fountainbridge is a kitchen story. 56 reviews at 4.59, level with July, negatives 12.5 per cent against 13.0 per cent. Twelve of its seventeen issues are food quality, the highest food share in Scotland.

The complaints are specific: five on taste, three on protein, two on broth. On 23/08/2026 a guest says the tonkotsu "broth was very thin and not at all creamy" with sinewy meat, and on 21/08/2026 another says "everything tastes stale and old".

This is an Executive Chef and BOH item before a GM one: broth density and chashu spec checked at the site, then held. Rory Ferguson owns stock rotation. Front of house is the strength, David named in 8 reviews.

month|2026-08|site|M6.text: Bath Street closed August at 4.52 on 25 reviews with 4 negatives, a 16.0% negative rate against the fleet's 6.0%. Small numbers, and the average is still ahead of July's 4.39 on 23 reviews. Service carries 3 of the 6 issue mentions: one rude or unfriendly attitude, one inattentive or forgotten, one bill or service charge. Food quality carries 2 and order sequencing 1. No dish and no staff member is named at this site in August, in praise or in complaint. Act on the rudeness: Justyna Polak (RM) to handle it directly, with Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh on coaching and rota. Watch the rest.

month|2026-08|site|M8.text:
Renfield's food is fine and its bill is not. 69 reviews at 4.65 against 51 at 4.63, negatives 8.7 per cent. Eleven of eighteen issues are service, and inside those four are the bill or service charge and three are a manager handling a complaint badly, the highest such count in the fleet.

On 04/08/2026 a returning customer writes "the manager was defensive throughout". On 29/08/2026 another reports a "10% tip to the receipt without even asking". A 09/08/2026 one star describes a £10 cocktail that was mostly ice, with the remedy refused.

Scott Renwick owns the complaint standard: listen, fix, remove the charge on request. Ka Ho should sit in on a shift. Behaviour, so act.

month|2026-08|site|MakiNori.text:
Maki Nori improved on every headline and still needs a fish check. 104 reviews at 4.72 against 73 at 4.62, negatives 11.0 per cent to 4.8 per cent, and Maki rolls praised 19 times, the site's clear strength.

Two reviews go the other way and both are freshness. On 15/08/2026 a guest says "the food was all stale, and the salmon actually smelled rotten". On 06/08/2026 another says the fish is not fresh and a piece fell out of a roll before service and was served anyway.

Executive Chef and BOH own a fish delivery, date and temperature check this week. The GM line still reads confirm, which Ziang Lin should close.

quarter|2026-Q3|fleet|.text:
The quarter's problem is service, not food, and it is worst in Scotland and Newcastle. Read Q3 as two months only: the pack covers 01/07/2026 to 31/08/2026 against a full 2026-Q2, so use rates and not totals.

Across 3,629 reviews the fleet sits at 4.75 stars and a 5.7% negative rate, which is Q2's 4.76 and 5.8% held flat. Underneath that the mix has moved. Food quality complaints per 100 reviews fell from 7.63 to 7.30, while service rose from 3.51 to 4.16, speed from 1.60 to 1.85, cleanliness from 1.73 to 1.98 and value from 1.39 to 1.54. The fastest riser is the bill: 32 service charge complaints against 21, on nearly every site's list.

Scotland and Newcastle is the outlier at 10.2% negative against 6.2%, on falling volume. The other two regions both improved.

Praise grew faster than reviews: 2,004 food and 1,864 service mentions, and Maki rolls stay the strongest dish at 97. Harvey (Manchester) 73, Navin (Shoreditch) 55, Mia (Southampton) 54 and Tinky (Southampton) 53 are the quarter's standouts and should be recognised by name.

Two owners: Ka Ho on Scotland, the Executive Chef on protein, where complaints rose from 33 to 43.

quarter|2026-Q3|region|Scotland & Newcas.text:
This region is the fleet's problem and it is quality first, service second. On 719 reviews the average fell to 4.63 from 4.74 and the negative rate went to 10.2% from 6.2%, the only region to worsen. Food quality complaints per 100 reviews rose from 6.98 to 10.29, service from 3.79 to 5.70 and speed from 1.35 to 2.50, so this is not a volume artefact.

Four sites are running at or near double the fleet negative rate: Nicolson 15.9%, Bath Street 14.6%, Fountainbridge 12.7% and Newcastle 11.8%. Aberdeen is the safety case, with three food safety mentions in July and August including two alleged food poisonings and a council complaint. Renfield has flipped to a service problem, with four manager handling complaints. Thirteen reviews object to the service charge, the highest rate in the fleet. Only SJQ Edinburgh improved, 11.3% to 5.7%.

Ka Ho as Head and Óisín Patrick Darragh as DAM own this: a taste and consistency pass with the Executive Chef at Nicolson, Fountainbridge and Newcastle, and complaint handling coaching at Renfield. Recognise Georgia (Newcastle) 8, David (Fountainbridge) 8 and Chris (Aberdeen) 7.

quarter|2026-Q3|region|North England & M.text:
Food is improving here and service is not. On 950 reviews the average held at 4.76 and the negative rate improved to 4.8% from 5.5%. Food quality complaints per 100 reviews fell from 7.61 to 7.05, but service rose from 2.83 to 4.84, the sharpest service deterioration of the three regions: 21 inattentive, eight rude and seven wrong or missing items.

Two of the five sites have no GM. At Meadowhall two 1-star reviews on 20/08/2026 and 24/08/2026 describe staff lecturing a family over the outside-food policy, one adding that the complaint email went unanswered. Nottingham carries 19 service issues and two long-wait reviews. There are two food safety mentions, a piece of plastic in the soup at Nottingham on 23/08/2026 and squid served with the membrane attached at Manchester on 28/08/2026. Manchester also refused an NHS card and a Groupon voucher in July, which is a policy question rather than a floor one. Leeds is a watch: 4.81 to 4.64 and three cold food complaints on small numbers (96 reviews).

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own the service recovery and the two GM vacancies. Recognise Harvey (Manchester) 73, Rami (Nottingham) 35 and James (Nottingham) 19.

quarter|2026-Q3|region|South England.text:
This is the region that improved, but most of the movement is new capacity, so treat the totals with care. On 1,960 reviews the average rose to 4.78 from 4.76 and the negative rate fell to 4.5% from 5.7%. Food quality complaints per 100 reviews fell from 8.03 to 6.33, service from 3.91 to 3.27 and sushi quality complaints from 19 to 12. Southampton (669 reviews), Shoreditch (403) and Maki 21 (203) supply most of the growth.

Two things went the wrong way. Cleanliness rose from 1.99 to 2.19 per 100 reviews, with 15 dirty premises mentions, and availability is the region's signature complaint at 16 sold out mentions, the highest in the fleet. There are three food safety mentions: contaminated edamame at Soho on 08/08/2026, tempura squid at Lakeside on 15/08/2026 and salmon that "actually smelled rotten" at Maki Nori on 15/08/2026.

Soho is the priority, 22 negatives at 9.8%. Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own the cleaning standard at Soho and Maki Nori and the availability question with the kitchens. Recognise Navin (Shoreditch) 55, Mia (Southampton) 54 and Tinky (Southampton) 53.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M1.text: Nicolson runs at 15.9% negative against a fleet 5.7%, the worst rate in the estate, on 44 reviews in two months, so these are small numbers. The average is 4.41 and it was 4.49 in Q2, so this is a standing position rather than a new fall. Eight of the 18 issues are food quality and five are taste, with two reviews comparing the site unfavourably with other branches: "some other locations are better food wise". Two service charge objections and two rudeness mentions complete it. Watch rather than act, but Derrick Cheung and Ka Ho should run a taste and consistency check against Fountainbridge with the Executive Chef.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M3.text: Fountainbridge is a food problem. The average fell to 4.59 from 4.72 and the negative rate to 12.7% from 7.3% on 102 reviews. Fifteen of the 29 issues are food quality: six taste, three portion, three protein and two broth. One review on 21/08/2026 reads "Everything tastes stale and old", and a second on 23/08/2026 says the tonkotsu broth is thin rather than creamy with sinewy meat. Four inattentive service mentions sit behind that. Rory Ferguson and the Executive Chef should re-check broth density and topping counts at this site specifically. David is praised eight times and is the site's strongest asset.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M6.text: Bath Street runs at 14.6% negative against 6.4% in Q2, with an average of 4.46 on 48 reviews, so small numbers and only four negative reviews in total. Three of the five food quality issues are taste and two are portion, with ramen described as sparsely topped on 25/07/2026 and 28/08/2026. The item to act on now is the review of 19/08/2026, where "the server was very rude, laughing to our faces" over a request for a spoon and plate that never arrived. Justyna Polak should hold that conversation this week. Everything else here is watch, not act, until the count builds.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M8.text: Renfield has flipped from a food site to a service site. Service is now the top category with 13 issues against six for food, and the negative rate is 8.3% against 4.6% in Q2 on 120 reviews. Four of those are manager handling: a lunch offer refused at 14:18 on 09/07/2026 with the GM backing the refusal, two reviews on 04/08/2026 including "the manager was defensive throughout the conversation", and a cocktail remedy refused on 09/08/2026. Four service charge objections attach to the same reviews. Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh should coach Scott Renwick on complaint handling and publish the lunch offer cut-off. Scott, Chloe and Kaz are all praised.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M12.text: Newcastle is 11.8% negative against 6.7%, average 4.68 on 76 reviews. Food quality is 15 of the 23 issues, with protein six and taste five. A returning family wrote on 12/07/2026: "Old overcooked noodles, small tasteless steak. Clumpy rice." Chicken ramen is named twice more, for watery broth on 15/08/2026 and dry bland chicken on 16/08/2026. Separately there are two door failures, entry refused at 21:15 on 13/08/2026 against a 22:00 close and wrong Monday hours online. Matt Lee owns the door; the Executive Chef owns the chicken ramen build; Becca should correct the Google listing hours. Georgia and Harry are the praised names.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M13.text: Aberdeen is a food safety case and should be acted on, not watched. The negative rate went to 9.6% from 3.1% and the average to 4.63 from 4.81 on 104 reviews. Three reviews carry food safety: spoiled soft shell crab and off rainbow roll on 06/07/2026 with reported food poisoning afterwards, a second alleged food poisoning with a council complaint on 12/07/2026, and gluten-free prawns fried in shared oil in an otherwise positive review. Three more cite dirty premises, including "Toilets were a pigsty and food was mediocre" on 18/07/2026. Executive Chef and BOH on fish handling and allergen separation, Joe Herera on toilets and menus. Chris is praised seven times.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M16.text: Nottingham improved to 6.0% negative from 8.9% and 4.72 from 4.62 on 217 reviews, but service is the standing fault: 19 issues, nine of them inattentive, two manager handling and two wrong or missing items. Waits recur, a takoyaki that never arrived inside an hour on 13/07/2026 and 30 minutes to order with one dish an hour behind the table on 23/08/2026. Two reviews carry food safety, "I found a piece of PLASTIC in the soup" on 23/08/2026 and a fly in a drink that Rami resolved. Filling the GM vacancy is the action for Inka Cheung. Rami 35, James 19 and Giovana 10 are carrying this site.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M17.text: Lakeside is one of the better sites, 3.9% negative on 283 reviews at 4.81, with food quality issues down from 31 to 19. Two items still need owners. On 15/08/2026 a guest reported that "the tempura squid tasted rotten" and asked for a refund, which the Executive Chef should trace to the batch. And three reviews describe guests ignored at the door or the table, on 19/07/2026 and 26/07/2026, with sticky menus noted again on 09/08/2026. Kei Cannon owns door cover and menu cleaning. Jocelyn is praised 29 times, Lera 19 and Maddison 14, which is a strong bench worth recognising.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M18.text: Soho is the fleet's priority site: 22 negative reviews, the highest count anywhere, a 9.8% rate against 7.3% and an average of 4.63 on 225 reviews. Food quality is 34 issues with 15 on taste, but cleanliness is what has changed, six dirty premises mentions including "the bar was covered in dirty glasses" on 08/08/2026 in a review that also reports contaminated edamame, out of order toilets on 25/08/2026 and a damp smell on 30/07/2026. Five staggered dish and four sold out mentions sit alongside. Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty with Imre Balogh on cleaning and pass discipline; Executive Chef on broth and steak.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M19.text: Shoreditch grew from 99 reviews to 403, so compare with care. The average is 4.77 and the negative rate 4.0%, both good, but 30 of the 52 issues are food quality and 14 of those are taste. On 02/08/2026 a guest wrote "The ramen had not depth of flavour but salt", with soggy karaage and inedible chashu in the same visit. Two door failures also stand out: the kitchen closed at 16:10 on 21/08/2026 against posted hours, and a booking taken before opening on 28/08/2026. Executive Chef on seasoning and chashu, Ziang Lin on confirming the GM, Becca on the posted hours. Navin 55, Jannat 28 and Amidu 18 are the praised names.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M20.text: Southampton delivered 669 reviews at 4.82 and only 3.3% negative, the largest feed in the fleet in its first proper quarter. It is an opening, not yet a performance, so read it as a promising start. The pattern in the 22 negatives is availability and sequencing: six sold out mentions ("lots of the menu was unavailable" on 14/07/2026), five staggered dishes and five inattentive. Nine comfort complaints are almost all heat and the lack of air conditioning, raised in five otherwise 5-star reviews, which is a building question. One coeliac party was promised accommodation and left without it on 11/08/2026. Mia 54, Tinky 53 and Yuya 17 are exceptional; one single negative naming is not a pattern.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|MakiNori.text: Maki Nori is moving the right way: 7.3% negative on 177 reviews against 10.9% on 285 in Q2, with the average up to 4.68 from 4.64. The residual is sushi and cleanliness. Eight sushi quality complaints include stale sushi on 31/07/2026 and, on 15/08/2026, "the salmon actually smelled rotten". Six dirty premises mentions run alongside, and two otherwise positive reviews still note an unclean cup and an uncleaned counter. Eight inattentive and eight overpriced complete the picture. Executive Chef and BOH on fish rotation and counter standards; the GM name is still to be confirmed, and Ziang Lin should close that.

month|2026-08|site|M9.text:
Manchester had the best month in the fleet and still has two kitchen handling failures worth naming. 385 reviews at 4.86 against 104 at 4.72, nine negatives at 2.3 per cent, 241 service praise mentions.

Both failures are about what happens after a guest complains. On 28/08/2026 a first time guest was served squid that "still had the membrane attached", felt nauseous, and was told the food arrives prepared and is only reheated, on a £90 bill. On 03/08/2026 a seafood hell ramen complaint was closed with the chef saying it was fine.

Executive Chef owns squid prep and the complaint response standard. Otherwise recognise this team: Harvey named in 70 reviews, Sam in 16, Tom in 11.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M15.text: Metrocentre doubled its negatives, four to 11, taking the rate to 9.2% from 3.8% on 120 reviews. The split is nine food quality and six service, with four inattentive, three staggered dishes and two slow bill mentions. The worst single visit, on 09/08/2026 at £72, describes noodles as "clearly pre heated grey pre packaged crap" with a tiny steak portion. Three further reviews describe chasing drinks, cutlery and the bill, and even 4 and 5-star reviews flag dishes landing at different times. Kieran Day owns pass sequencing and section cover; Óisín Patrick Darragh should look at the rota. Only two praise mentions here, which is thin.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M10.text: Leeds is 4.64 on 96 reviews in a quarter that is only two months in, against 4.81 on 199 across a full Q2. On rate that is about 48 reviews a month against 66 in Q2, and the negative rate has gone from 4.0% to 7.3% while the fleet held near 5.7%. Food quality carries 10 of the 17 issue mentions: general taste 3, food cold or lukewarm 3, broth 2, protein 2. Egg and steak are each named twice. Value adds 3 on price. Ninder Joshi on pass to table time, with Inka Cheung and Amy Tang; Executive Chef on the broth. Recognition: Leandra 8, Gaby 7.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M11.text: Leicester is at 9.1% negative against 5.5%, average 4.56 on 77 reviews, so small numbers but a clear pattern. Protein is the theme: six of the 13 food quality issues, with a hard-boiled ramen egg, burnt pork katsu and shredded pork instead of slices on 24/07/2026, and boiled flavourless chicken on 18/08/2026. Service adds seven issues, six of them inattentive, including two 1-star visits on 03/08/2026 and 04/08/2026 that both name dirty tables and an unavailable ramen. One guest wrote "Skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow". Executive Chef on protein prep; Inka Cheung and Amy Tang on peak cover with Caroline and JJ.

week|2026-08-17|site|M9.text: 195 reviews, average 4.93, one negative, against 101 at 4.93. This is the fleet's largest review base and, at 0.5%, its lowest negative rate. Harvey was named in 60 reviews, Aiden in 6, Mia in 5 and Sam in 4: a recognition item for Inka Cheung and Amy Tang this week, not a performance one. The only repeated theme is the room, three mentions of noise and decor inside otherwise positive reviews, "Music a little too loud". The food notes are minor, a steak ramen under-spiced and a chicken ramen broth called mediocre. Sales met target and the site moved from red to green on the red light system. Nothing to act on beyond music volume.

month|2026-08|site|M21.text:
Maki 21 opened during August, so this is a part month against whole months everywhere else and there is no July comparison. Judge nothing on it. As a rate, 203 reviews at 4.89 with five negatives at 2.5 per cent is the fleet's highest average. Elham is praised in 19 reviews, Charlotte and Felicia in 7 each.

Three things to carry, not act on. A one star on 22/08/2026 describes management as hostile to returning guests, and a five star review names manager Nicky as snappy at the door. One review on 24/08/2026 reports illness, logged under food safety.

Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own door manner coaching and the GM vacancy.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M9.text: Manchester is the region's best result. On 489 reviews the negative rate halved to 2.9% from 5.0% and the average rose to 4.83, with food quality issues down from 30 to 14. Two things remain. Offers were refused twice in July, an NHS card on 06/07/2026 and a Groupon voucher on 19/07/2026, both handled dismissively, which is a policy fix not a floor one. And on 28/08/2026 a guest had "the squid which still had the membrane attached" and felt unwell on a £90 bill, which the Executive Chef should trace. Harvey is praised 73 times, the highest in the fleet, with Sam 16 and Aiden 14.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M14.text: Meadowhall has no GM and a repeat behaviour to correct. The negative rate is 7.0% against 5.4% on 71 reviews, so small numbers, but two 1-star reviews on 20/08/2026 and 24/08/2026 describe the same thing: staff lecturing a family condescendingly over the outside-food policy, with the second adding that a complaint email went unanswered. That is rudeness plus an unclosed complaint, so it is act rather than watch. Inka Cheung and Amy Tang should issue a plain script for the outside-food policy and name who answers complaint email while the GM post is open. Jemma is the only praised name, three mentions.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M21.text: Maki 21 opened in August, so its 203 reviews cover roughly one month of the quarter and there is no prior period to compare. On that short window it holds the fleet's best average at 4.89 and 2.5% negative, with 133 food and 132 service praise mentions. A new site is not judged on a short window, so this is encouraging rather than proven. All three negative reviews fall after 22/08/2026: a manager described as hostile to returning guests with chairs stacked during service, an order not taken for 10 minutes on 24/08/2026 with illness reported afterwards, and one overpriced ramen. Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty should appoint the GM and coach the duty manager. Elham is praised 19 times.

week|2026-08-24|fleet|.text:
The week's problem is food, not people, and it is spread across all three regions rather than parked in one. Reviews fell to 462 from 554 in the week to 17/08/2026, the average slipped from 4.84 to 4.69, and the negative share more than doubled, 3.6 per cent to 7.6 per cent. Food quality is the largest issue category at 47 mentions against 28 prior, and general taste complaints alone moved from 9 to 24.

Three of those are food safety and need answering first. Aberdeen on 26/08/2026: karaage out in 60 seconds with "red pieces, appearing jelly like and under cooked". Manchester on 28/08/2026: squid served with the membrane on, guest left nauseous. Maki 21 on 24/08/2026: two guests reported illness after steak ramen. Executive Chef owns the cook and probe checks at all three, with each GM on the day.

Steak is the most complained dish at 6 mentions across four sites, usually overcooked or thin, so treat it as a spec and supply question, not one kitchen. Second theme is the bill: 6 complaints about a service charge added without consent, at Aberdeen, Renfield, Metrocentre, Manchester and Meadowhall.

Volume also collapsed at Manchester (195 to 46) and Leeds (22 to 4). Becca to check the Google feed.

week|2026-08-24|region|Scotland & Newcas.text:
Scotland and Newcastle held its rating (4.64 against 4.70) on rising volume, 97 reviews against 74, but the negative rate crept up to 10.3 per cent from 9.5 per cent and the region now has the fleet's clearest money and manners problem: 4 value complaints, 4 on price and 3 on the bill itself.

The one item to act on is Aberdeen, 26/08/2026, where karaage arrived in 60 seconds and the guest describes red, jelly like pieces. That is food safety: Executive Chef and Joe Herera to check fryer timings and probe records this week. Everything else is coaching. Metrocentre and Renfield both took complaints about a 10 per cent tip added unasked, Fountainbridge took a hygiene and attitude review on 26/08/2026, and taste alone drew 6 mentions across Bath Street, SJQ Edinburgh, Nicolson and Metrocentre. None of those sites is trading badly.

Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh own two things: one script for how the service charge is presented, identical across the region, and a taste and topping check at the small Edinburgh and Glasgow sites. Recognition is easy this week: Peter, Jezer and Chris at Aberdeen took 7 named mentions between them, and Newcastle scored a clean 5.0 on 8 reviews.

week|2026-08-24|region|North England & M.text:
Read this region's numbers with the volume caveat first. It filed 72 reviews against 244 the week before, so the average of 4.49 (from 4.88) and the 11.1 per cent negative rate sit on a much smaller base. Manchester dropped from 195 reviews to 46, Leeds from 22 to 4 and Nottingham from 17 to 6. That collection drop is itself a job for Becca before the next pull.

On the reviews that did land, the problem is service and handling more than food. Meadowhall carries three of the eight negatives, including a 24/08/2026 review describing rude and condescending handling of the outside food policy and a complaint email that went unanswered. Its labour hours rose 572.8 to 666.7 and sales beat target by 8.37 per cent, so this is handling, not headcount. Leicester is the worst rated site in the fleet at 3.20, on small numbers, with hours down 429.4 to 415.0 and a review reading "Skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow". Manchester's 28/08/2026 squid review is food safety and goes to Executive Chef.

Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own the Meadowhall reply and door, and the Leicester rota. Harvey (8 mentions), Tom (4) and Jazmin (3) carried Manchester.

week|2026-08-24|region|South England.text:
South England has the fleet's best negative rate at 5.8 per cent on much the largest sample, 293 reviews, but the rate still rose from 3.4 per cent and the average eased 4.83 to 4.76. The problem here is food: 27 of the region's issues are food quality, with 13 on taste and 4 on food arriving cold or lukewarm.

It concentrates in two sites. Soho took 4 negatives on 41 reviews, with filthy and out of order toilets on 25/08/2026 and ramen "incredibly salty" plus a sticky table on 30/08/2026, and its KPIs agree: food cost 30.61 per cent from 21.09 per cent, efficiency 51, red light red. Shoreditch carries 9 food quality issues and its service complaints land on a week when labour hours fell 431.7 to 390.9. Maki 21 is in its opening period and should not be judged on it, but the 24/08/2026 illness report is a food safety item for Executive Chef.

Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own the Soho clean down and the Shoreditch rota. Recognition: Navin at Shoreditch was named 19 times, Elham at Maki 21 13, Jada at Maki Nori 6, Imi at Soho 4.

week|2026-08-24|site|M9.text: Manchester filed 46 reviews at 4.70, down from 195 at 4.93, and only 2 were negative (4.3 per cent), so the rating is not the story. The 28/08/2026 one star is: squid served with the membrane still attached, the guest told the food "comes in prepared" and is only fried or heated, and left feeling nauseous. That is a food safety and prep item for Executive Chef with Kai Chau Leung and Chan Zhi Quan, this week not next. A four star also flags dirty toilets and menus. Trading is fine, efficiency 98 and sales 2.13 per cent above target. Harvey (8), Tom (4) and Jazmin (3) were the named servers. Becca to chase why volume fell so far.

week|2026-08-24|site|M11.text: Leicester averaged 3.20 on 5 reviews, down from 4.62 on 8, with 2 negatives. Small numbers, so this is watch rather than act, but both one stars say the same thing. One reports tasteless ramen, steak overcooked against a medium rare request and an egg that was not runny. The other reports long waits, lukewarm food and a slow bill: "Skeleton staff meant that service was extremely slow". Labour hours fell 429.4 to 415.0 on sales close to target, so the speed complaint and the rota point the same way. Caroline and JJ to walk the Friday and Saturday deployment with Inka Cheung and Amy Tang, and Executive Chef to re-check the steak cook.

week|2026-08-24|site|M13.text: Aberdeen looks healthy on the face of it: 22 reviews at 4.59, up from 8, with 14 service praises and Peter (3), Jezer (2) and Chris (2) named. It is here for one review. On 26/08/2026 a guest reports karaage arriving within 60 seconds and biting into red, jelly like pieces they judged undercooked, alongside sticky menus and a dried out egg. Undercooked chicken is not a rating question, so Joe Herera and Executive Chef own it now: fryer timings, batch holding and probe records for the week, plus a menu wipe down added to the open. The second negative is only a service charge objection. Efficiency 88 amber, food cost 20.66 per cent, nothing else to chase.

week|2026-08-24|site|M14.text: Meadowhall has the lowest average of any site with a real sample: 4.00 on 11 reviews, 3 negatives at 27.3 per cent against a fleet 7.6 per cent. Service carries 4 of its 8 issues. The 24/08/2026 one star describes a staff member being rude and condescending about the outside food policy, which the family says they would have accepted if explained politely, plus an unanswered complaint email. Another reports a long door wait with empty tables, a third a ramen with very little broth. Hours rose 572.8 to 666.7 and sales beat target by 8.37 per cent: this is handling, not cover. The GM post is vacant, so Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own the reply and the door.

week|2026-08-24|site|M15.text: Metrocentre came in at 4.48 on 21 reviews, just under the 4.5 line on a sample big enough to mean it, with 3 negatives. Two of the three are about money rather than the meal: a tip added to the bill without consent on 28/08/2026, and a straight price comparison against a competitor. The third, on 24/08/2026, is mediocre food with forgetful service and no regular soy sauce on offer. Trading is strong, sales 21.68 per cent above target on 3,239 covers and efficiency 95 green, so this is a till and script fix, not a performance issue. Kieran Day to brief how the service charge is introduced, and to get standard soy sauce back on the floor.

week|2026-08-24|site|M18.text: Soho took 4 negatives on 41 reviews (9.8 per cent) and its reviews and its KPIs are telling one story. Food quality carries 5 issues and cleanliness 3: filthy and out of order toilets on 25/08/2026, then a sticky table with ramen "incredibly salty" and greasy black garlic oil on 30/08/2026,. Food cost jumped 21.09 to 30.61 per cent, wage is 26.06 per cent, efficiency 51 and red light red, on labour hours up 637.4 to 664.7. Imre Balogh owns the toilet and table checks today. Executive Chef owns seasoning and oil on the black garlic. Imi (4), Raj (3) and Ginger (2) were named well: the floor is not short of good people.

week|2026-08-24|site|M19.text: Shoreditch filed 63 reviews at 4.65 with 5 negatives, broadly flat on the prior week, but food quality now carries 9 issues: tempura twice, maki rolls twice, thin well done steak, overcooked sushi rice and a greasy lukewarm yakisoba on 30/08/2026. On service, hours fell 431.7 to 390.9 and the complaints follow: a booked table ignored for 10 minutes, "Had to steal cutlery because nobody brought us any", and a 40 minute wait for food. A guest accepted for a 4pm booking on 28/08/2026 arrived to a closed restaurant. With the GM post TBC, Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own the rota and the booking window. Navin was named 19 times, the most praised person in the fleet.

week|2026-08-24|site|M21.text:
Maki 21 filed 107 reviews, the largest feed in the fleet, at 4.85 against 4.94 prior, with 4 negatives at 3.7 per cent. It is in its opening period, so treat none of that as a performance read.

One item needs acting on. On 24/08/2026 two guests reported diarrhoea after steak ramen, in a review that also describes very salty chicken and a 10 minute wait before anyone took the order. Executive Chef owns the cook temperature and holding records for that day. Steak drew 3 complaints and beef ramen 2, so the protein is worth a spec check. Recognition is the other half: Elham was named 13 times, Felicia 6, and Norah, Aiden and Adan 4 each.

week|2026-08-17|site|M14.text: Small numbers, 2 reviews and an average of 3.0, but the negative is behaviour. On 20/08/2026 a family who had brought a small amount of food for a young daughter were told she could not eat it, and the complaint is the condescending way it was put, not the policy. Six issues are logged across the two reviews, including portion size, a roll mix up and difficulty flagging staff on the lower level, all raised inside a 5-star. The GM post is vacant, so Inka Cheung and Amy Tang own how the policy is explained and a named lead on shift. Sales were 8.4% under target, but the site moved from red to green on the red light system.

week|2026-08-17|site|M21.text: Read this as an opening period, not a performance. 96 reviews at 4.94, one negative (1.0%) and no prior week for comparison. The praise is heavy: food in 63 reviews, service in 61 and the room in 33, with Elham named 6 times and Charlotte 4. The one negative, on 22/08/2026, is a guest who had left 5 stars and dropped to 1 after a late evening return, describing the manager as hostile and chairs stacked while people were still eating. Closing down behaviour is worth correcting early, before it sets. Ziang Lin and Kaitlin Docherty own that while the GM post is vacant. Wage at 52.49% and efficiency at 34 are opening figures, not a read on the team.
